correctness.summary: Rayleigh quotient bounds place BB2, BB1, and every interval selector inside [1/L,1/mu]. The A-energy error operator therefore gives the global objective-gap factor (kappa-1)^2. A two-dimensional endpoint construction beginning with an exact line-search step makes BB1 and BB2 simultaneously approach 1/mu while the current gradient approaches the L-eigenmode, so every selector in the shrinking interval has gap ratio tending to (kappa-1)^2. This proves sharpness and the exact monotonicity frontier kappa<=2. Deterministic numerical checks reproduce all formulas and bounds.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical BB sources, Raydan's nonmonotonicity and globalization work, R-linear convergence theory, the convex BB1/BB2 spectral family, later surveys and harmonic-Rayleigh formulations, and recent sharp asymptotic/Lyapunov analyses were checked. Searches for exact or synonymous statements did not locate the condition-number frontier kappa=2, the sharp one-step objective amplification (kappa-1)^2, or the fact that every selector between BB2 and BB1 can be forced to increase after an exact-line-search warm-up. Complete theorem-level text of some broad historical sources was not inspected in full, leaving residual prior-coverage risk.

value.summary: The result converts qualitative BB nonmonotonicity into an exact conditioning boundary and sharp excursion size, while showing that adaptive blending anywhere between the two canonical BB steps cannot restore universal descent above the boundary. The exact-line-search warm-up makes the obstruction independent of an artificially poor initial step.

limitations: Finite-dimensional real SPD quadratics and exact arithmetic only.
The claim concerns objective-gap monotonicity, not gradient-norm or iterate-norm monotonicity.
Selectors outside the contemporaneous BB2-BB1 interval, clipping, line searches, trust regions, and other globalization devices are not covered.
The threshold is a uniform worst-case guarantee; particular trajectories may remain monotone for kappa>2.
No new asymptotic convergence rate, iteration complexity, or implementation-performance claim is made.
Complete theorem-level access to some broad historical BB sources was not obtained, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
